**No.** This excerpt is mainly scene-setting: it describes the shop sign, the rapeseed sacks, the wagon's route and the layout of the hallway. The characters get very little development.

- **Abel Hradscheck** is the only figure with any shading. His instructions, and his knowing remark that "Kätzchen" (Quaas's wife) likes compliments, hint at a shrewd, socially calculating man. Beyond that, he remains a sketch of a businessman.
- **Jakob**, the farmhand, only nods, says a sleepy "Hüh", and drives the wagon out of the scene. He is purely functional, there to carry out the errand and move the action along.
- **Ölmüller Quaas, his wife, and Leist in Wrietzen** are only names, mentioned to set up the business transaction.

Since several figures appear only to serve the logistics of the scene, the story does not meet the standard that no character feels present simply to satisfy a plot requirement.
